subject: Re: DPA — output metadata & subprocessors (telemetry exclusion request)
messages:
From: Emma Wong <emma.wong@stellar.ai>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
Cc: legal <legal@stellar.ai>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DPA redline — request to exclude output metadata from telemetry

Hi Michael,

Thanks for the call yesterday. We attached our proposed DPA redline (v3) — two items need confirmation from product/security before we can proceed:

1) Output metadata exclusion: We ask that any customer-generated outputs (including model completions and downstream text) not be included in telemetry that is processed by any subprocessor. Stellar's legal is requesting an explicit carve-out: "Customer outputs and derived customer content shall not be used for telemetry, training, or analytics by Redwood or any subprocessor."

2) Subprocessor list and KV/cache behavior: We want confirmation that temporary KV caches or telemetry snapshots retained for optimization do not include customer outputs, and a promise to notify us if a new analytics subprocessor will process any runtime outputs.

We can accept limited operational telemetry (resource metrics, token counts) but not payload-level outputs. Attached redline shows the exact text.

Can you confirm whether product/security will sign off or whether you need a mitigation (e.g., contract language plus an operational control)? We have a planned signature window for next week.

Thanks,
Emma Wong
Legal Counsel, Stellar AI
Attachments: Stellar_DPA_redline_v3.pdf, redline_diff.docx

---

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wong <emma.wong@stellar.ai>
Cc: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — request to exclude output metadata from telemetry

Emma —

Thanks for sending the redlines and for being explicit about the scope. Looping in Olga (Product) and Rishi (Security) to assess product impact and whether the legal language is acceptable as-is or requires an operational supplement.

Quick context for our side: Redwood's baseline telemetry includes metrics (latency, GPU utilization, token counts) and error traces. We do sometimes collect anonymized samples of outputs for debugging rare failures and quality regressions, but those samples are filtered and access-controlled.

Next steps from my side: Olga/Rishi, can you comment on two ask areas: (A) whether we can commit contractually to never include full customer outputs in telemetry sent to downstream analytics subprocessors, and (B) what product-level mitigations (config flags, opt-out, manual QA-only sampling with customer approval) we can offer without breaking our ability to debug and maintain models?

If we can get a short proposed clause or an operational playbook, I will return to Emma with a final position. We are under sign-off pressure from their procurement.

—Michael
Head of Solutions & Partnerships
Redwood Inference

---

From: Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Emma Wong <emma.wong@stellar.ai>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 13:18:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — request to exclude output metadata from telemetry

Hi all,

Thanks for the clear ask, Emma. From a product standpoint I want to be explicit about what we can and cannot promise without introducing significant support overhead or impacting model quality monitoring:

- Contractual commitment: We can accept a clause that prohibits telemetry vendors and analytics subprocessors from using full customer outputs for training or commercial analytics. We would prefer language that allows for "limited, access-controlled debug samples" with explicit customer opt-in. Suggested clause language: "Redwood and its subprocessors will not use Customer outputs for model training or analytics. Narrow exceptions for access-controlled, minimal debug samples (not exceeding X samples per month) may be used only for troubleshooting and require Customer consent or prior notice."

- Operational controls: We can implement a per-account control (toggle) to disable output-level telemetry sampling at runtime for customers who require it. That will prevent any accidental capture in future analytics exports. Implementation estimate: 2–3 sprints to add a per-account flag plus UI/API config and update our telemetry export pipeline to respect it.

- KV cache / prefix caching: The KV cache is strictly runtime and not persisted to long-term analytics; however, temporary snapshots currently feed into internal model perf tooling. We can patch the pipelines so that KV/cache snapshots exclude user outputs. That would be a low-risk software change (1 sprint) and can be confirmed in the ops playbook.

- Exposure to subprocessors: We maintain a list of analytics subprocessors and can add requirement to notify customers 30 days prior to onboarding any new subprocessor that will have access to telemetry.

If Stellar accepts the opt-in for debug sampling and we ship the per-account disable flag as part of the contract side commitments, I think we can get to "green" without changing our core monitoring. Rishi — please confirm security implications below.

Thanks,
Olga
Head of Product — Runtime
Redwood Inference

---

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Emma Wong <emma.wong@stellar.ai>
Cc: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — request to exclude output metadata from telemetry

Emma, Michael —

Security sign-off summary: we can accept a prohibition on using customer outputs for training or analytics, provided two operational commitments are made and documented in a security playbook:

1) Per-account telemetry disable: As Olga said, we will add a per-account runtime flag that prevents output-level samples from being captured and exported. This will be gated so only our ops team can enable/disable and will be visible in the account audit log.

2) Access & retention controls: Any retained debug samples must be encrypted-at-rest, access-controlled (RBAC), and subject to a 30-day retention default unless customer explicitly approves longer retention for a debug window. We will update our subprocessor contracts to include non-use clauses for outputs and notify customers 30 days before a new analytics subprocessor processes telemetry for their account.

If Stellar can accept these operational commitments written into the DPA (and opt-in language for debug sampling), Security will sign off. Please let us know if the 30-day notification window or the 30-day retention default is acceptable — we can negotiate those numbers.

—Rishi
Chief Security Officer
Redwood Inference

---

From: Michael Grant <michael_grant@redwood.com>
To: Emma Wong <emma.wong@stellar.ai>, Olga Petrov <olga_petrov@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 26 Apr 2027 15:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DPA redline — request to exclude output metadata from telemetry

Emma —

Thanks for the patience. Summary and next steps:

1) Proposed contract language (short): "Redwood and its subprocessors will not use Customer outputs for model training or analytics. Limited, access-controlled debug samples may be collected only with Customer consent; such samples will be encrypted, access-controlled, and retained by default no longer than 30 days."

2) Operational commitments: implement per-account telemetry disable flag (ETA: 2–3 sprints), patch KV/cache snapshot filters (1 sprint), update subprocessor contracts and 30-day notification. Security will include these in the security playbook and sign off after we add the per-account flag and retention language.

3) Timeline / ask for Stellar: If the DPA includes the clause above and acknowledges the operational commitments with delivery windows, can Stellar accept that and proceed to signature? If yes, I will circulate a short redline back to legal today.

Ben — please prep the minimal redline text and I will send to Emma.

—Michael

Michael —

Thanks for the clear summary. Stellar can accept the proposed language and the operational commitments below, provided we receive: (1) a redline that includes the short clause above, (2) an explicit timeline for the per-account flag and KV/cache patch, and (3) written confirmation that debug samples will require explicit customer consent before collection. If you can get that back to us today or tomorrow, Procurement will proceed with signature.

I look forward to Ben's redline.

Best,
Emma
Legal Counsel, Stellar AI
summary: External legal requested exclusion of customer outputs from telemetry. Internal thread coordinated product and security to accept contract clause plus operational commitments: per-account telemetry disable (2–3 sprints), KV/cache filter (1 sprint), 30-day retention default for debug samples, and 30-day notice for new subprocessors. Redline to be prepared and returned to customer for signature.
